subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Despite the challenges, / the team is determined to / completed / the project on time and within budget.

options.text: the project on time and within budget

solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. completed .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence contains a grammatical error in the segment "**completed**".
 
• The verb "**completed**" is incorrect in this context because the sentence uses the phrase "**the team is determined to**", which requires the base form of the verb (infinitive without "to").
 
• The correct form should be "**complete**" instead of "**completed**".
 
• The correct structure is "**to + base form of the verb**", which aligns with the grammatical rule for verbs following "determined to".

Correct sentence: *Despite the challenges, the team is determined to **complete** the project on time and within budget.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common error in verb usage:**
 
 
• When a verb follows phrases like "**determined to**", "**want to**", or "**need to**", always use the base form of the verb.
 
• **Example:** She is determined to **win** the competition (not "winning" or "won").
 
 
 
• **How to identify such errors:**
 
 
• Look for auxiliary verbs like "**is**", "**was**", "**determined to**", and check if the following verb is in its correct base form.
